claims.statement: Messages is a single-APK Kotlin/Jetpack-Compose Android app that is simultaneously (a) a full default SMS/MMS app (Compose UI, onboarding, quick replies, drafts, blocklist, app lock, search, backup) and (b) an embedded self-hosted SMS/MMS gateway: a LAN HTTP REST server (default port 8080) plus a webhook engine; it targets minSdk 26 (Android 8.0+), targetSdk/compileSdk 36, and is currently versionName 2.6.19 / versionCode 61. It is a heavily extended fork of manjitrana/Messages.

The only Gradle module is :app (root project name "Messages"); its namespace and applicationId are both com.autonomousone.messages, and dependency versions are centralized in the gradle/libs.versions.toml catalog (AGP 8.10.1, Kotlin 2.2.10, KSP, Room 2.8.4).

./gradlew assembleDebug builds the debug APK (app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk) and ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest runs the headless JVM unit-test suite; build-debug.yml (push/PR to master or main, Temurin JDK 17) runs exactly these two commands and uploads the debug APK, making it the only workflow that runs unit tests, while release.yml triggers on v* tags, builds the signed release APK, and publishes the GitHub Release.

The Gradle property -PGATEWAY_BACKEND_URL overrides the default https://gaitway.autonomousone.in baked into the generated BuildConfig.GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL build field, and BuildConfig.APP_VERSION is derived from versionName as the single version source; at runtime GatewayPreferences.backendUrl prefers the user-configured setting and falls back to BuildConfig.GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL, enforcing HTTPS-only values.

The system Telephony content providers are the durable source of truth: MessagesDatabase is an explicitly labeled local read-SSOT shadow that the UI reads from, and IncomingMessageDispatcher fans out every received message from the persisted provider row's real id + threadId (not broadcast extras) so UI, webhooks, and notifications all react to provider state.

The manifest wires the default-SMS-app surface: singleTask MainActivity with sms:/smsto:/mms:/mmsto: SENDTO and text/plain SEND intent filters; SmsReceiver with priority-999 SMS_RECEIVED and SMS_DELIVER filters; vendored mmslib PushReceiver (WAP_PUSH_DELIVER) and TransactionService; HeadlessSmsSendService for the required RESPOND_VIA_MESSAGE action; manifest-lifetime SmsStatusReceiver for durable SENT/DELIVERED callbacks; and the non-exported GatewayService foreground service (foregroundServiceType dataSync|specialUse). The application disables allowBackup (the app ships its own XML backup/restore instead).

Gateway startup and transmission are consent-gated by GatewayAccessPolicy (canStart requires versioned user consent; canTransmit requires consent AND the runtime enabled flag), and revoking consent clears the enabled/desired flags, auto-start, and cloud credentials; GatewayService.startGateway silently refuses to start without consent.

GatewayPreferences splits user intent from runtime state: gatewayDesiredEnabled is the persisted intent that start/stop flips and that survives reboot, while the isEnabled flag is a runtime mirror written only by ConnectionSupervisor; BootGatewayReceiver replays ACTION_START on BOOT_COMPLETED only when desired intent and consent both persist, so the gateway self-recovers after reboot with no manual step.

The REST gateway authenticates every request with the gateway API key (format gw_ + 32 hex chars, generated on first launch and stored encrypted with the Android Keystore via SecureStore with transparent migration of legacy plaintext), and hardens against abuse with per-IP brute-force lockout (8 consecutive failed auth attempts within 10 minutes triggers a 5-minute lockout) plus DoS caps (1 MB request body, 100 headers, 32 KB header block).

GatewayServer is a hand-rolled ServerSocket-based HTTP server (Android lacks com.sun.net.httpserver), using a single-thread acceptor and an 8-thread handler pool so slow handlers cannot starve accept(); it serves the /api/v1/* endpoints (sms/send, mms/send, sms/inbox, sms, status, sms/schedule CRUD), the EVE provider contract paths (/send, /send/status/{id}, /send/cancel/{id}, /send/capacity), and unauthenticated /health plus /ready readiness checks.

The gateway's outbound bridges are: BackendClient (central HTTPS-only HTTP client with Bearer token auth, 15s/30s timeouts, for the optional cloud relay register/heartbeat/event flow), WebhookEngine (fire-and-forget, consent-gated POST of incoming SMS to a user-configured HTTPS webhook with HMAC-SHA256 X-Signature plus idempotent cloud event upload), and OutboxPoller (outbound-only GMweb long-poll bridge: GET /gateway/pull then POST /gateway/ack, authenticated with the phone's own gateway API key, delivering polled tasks through EveSmsQueue).

EveSmsQueue is the persistent priority send-queue implementing the EVE "Custom HTTP" provider contract: it maps an Idempotency-Key to a stable requestId, processes messages highest-priority-first on a single worker, and tracks status QUEUED → ACTIVE → SENT|FAILED (or CANCELLED).

The quality gate is a headless JUnit 4 unit-test suite under app/src/test (junit 4.13.2 is the only test dependency; no Robolectric), which runs on a bare JVM because testOptions sets unitTests.isReturnDefaultValues = true so Android APIs like android.util.Log no-op; the instrumented suite under app/src/androidTest is a single placeholder, so device-bound behavior (MMS receivers, the live gateway, ContentObserver) is verified on a device or emulator.

The mmslib MMS stack is vendored as app/libs/mmslib-1.0.0.aar with its three POM runtime dependencies declared explicitly in the version catalog (file dependencies carry no transitive metadata), because JitPack — its only remote publication — has repeated CI-breaking outages and is deliberately absent from every Gradle repository; the Aliyun mirror in settings.gradle.kts is a scoped last-resort fallback for Google/Android artifacts only.

Release signing reads KEYSTORE_FILE/KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/KEY_ALIAS/KEY_PASSWORD from environment (CI) or a gitignored keystore.properties (local), and degrades to an unsigned build when no keystore is present; all keystores and keystore.properties are gitignored, release.yml decodes a base64 keystore secret into keystore.jks before assembling, and scripts/generate-release-metadata.ps1 emits the APK SHA-256 and signer certificate SHA-256 for Play Protect appeals.

AGENTS.md binds the repo's working conventions: source code and tests are authoritative over documentation; generated openwiki/ pages must not be hand-edited (a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow regenerates the wiki, so change source/docs and let it re-run); and the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior is preferred, with complete failure output preserved.

Room schemas are exported to app/schemas via the KSP room.schemaLocation argument (exported JSON currently spans versions 2 through 6, matching MessagesDatabase version 6), and the schema JSON files are build artifacts of history that must never be hand-edited; destructive fallback migration is intentional while the shadow remains non-authoritative and rebuildable from the provider.

First-run device flow: install the APK on an Android 8.0+ phone with an active SIM, complete onboarding (accept disclosure → set as default SMS app → grant SMS/Contacts permissions), then enable the gateway via 3-Dots Menu → SMS Gateway and copy the API key; the REST API is then reachable at http://<phone-ip>:8080 (X-API-Key auth), and scripts/test-gateway-api.ps1 live-smoke-tests every documented endpoint read-only by default with real SMS/MMS sends opt-in.

openwiki/ is a generated evidence index maintained by the daily (06:00 UTC) openwiki-update.yml workflow, which checks out with full history, runs openwiki code --update, and opens a PR touching openwiki/, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and the workflow itself — the stated reason hand-editing wiki pages is discouraged.
